page: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The AMD EPYC 9V45 processor achieves top-tier status in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, due to the low core count of 2 vCPUs, multi-threaded performance scales down significantly. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, static web serving throughput, and the overall PassMark CPU score fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET operations at 6.72 million operations per second, perform in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F8-2amds_v7 offers high memory density and fast single-threaded execution without the overhead of a high core count. This makes it a specialized option for workloads that require substantial memory capacity but do not scale well across multiple threads. Conversely, the server exhibits poor performance in multi-threaded compiling, ray tracing, and medium-sized LLM inference. The hardware profile is best suited for memory-intensive single-threaded applications, lightweight database operations, caching layers, and text processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 2 physical cores, 2 vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD. The server exhibits top-tier single-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core benchmarks. However, multi-threaded scaling is a notable tradeoff, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput falling into the bottom 25%. Caching and memory bandwidth benchmarks remain average, with Redis SET operations reaching 6.72 million operations per second. This resource profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-dense, single-threaded workloads, lightweight database operations, and text processing, but is poorly suited for highly parallelized compute tasks or large-scale LLM inference.
